title: Chapter 10
paragraphs: From then on, a new kind of life began for Alexey Alexandrovitch and his wife. Nothing dramatic happened. Anna kept going out in society as she always had, was especially often at Princess Betsy's, and ran into Vronsky everywhere. Alexey Alexandrovitch saw it, but there was nothing he could do about it. Every attempt he made to draw her into an open conversation ran up against a wall he couldn't get through — a kind of amused bewilderment on her part. On the surface, nothing had changed, but underneath, their relationship was completely different. Alexey Alexandrovitch, a man with real power in the world of politics, found himself powerless here. Like an ox with its head lowered, he waited submissively for the blow he sensed hanging over him. Every time he thought about it, he told himself he had to try once more — that kindness, tenderness, and persuasion might still save her, might still bring her back to herself — and every day he got ready to talk to her. But every time he actually started, he felt that the same spirit of deceit and wrongdoing that had taken hold of her had taken hold of him too, and he ended up speaking to her in a completely different tone than he'd meant to use. Without meaning to, he fell into his habitual tone of mocking anyone who said what he was about to say. And in that tone, there was no way to say what actually needed to be said to her.
